rv.q: This show remains a stunning piece of theatre: an immensely moving response to the futility of war.
Joey remains a masterpiece of creativity and connection.
Actually it turns out War Horse is still incredible.
The show never fails to move me to tears, not least because of its improbability.

As long as War Horse exists, the National will be fine.
This adaptation by Nick Stafford in association with Handspring Puppet Company is – on so many levels – a tour de force.
War Horse is a theatrical masterpiece.
This is theatre and theatrical invention at its finest.

With Albert determined to reunite with his horse, he sets out on a remarkable journey across the front lines, clutching a sketch of Joey as his guide and constant reminder of home. Led by the rich, evocative vocals of Sally Swanson, the ensemble works seamlessly to transport us into the heart of the conflict.
Hell yeah! ...The show stands as a rip-roaring and astounding achievement in theatre and (bizarrely) looks fresher and more vibrant than it did nearly 20 years ago.
War Horse remains relevant because big men still go to war, and a lot of people suffer for it.
War Horse remains relevant because big men still go to war, and a lot of people suffer for it. But as the remarkable and rather moving conclusion brings two old friends back together, hope remains.
So all the equine and puppetry magic is there, undimmed in two decades: a national treasure and global theatrical pride.
War Horse is just as magical and inspiring as it ever was.
Tom Sturgess is just perfect – fresh-faced, smiling, finally haunted – as Albert.
Joey is magnificent, a puppet that doesn't attempt to hide the three humans controlling him yet utterly convinces you that he is indeed a horse.
All-in-all, these gripes with the script and acting choices don't take away from the overall power of the production.
War Horse is a story of triumph, trust, and innocent love; a must-see.
This is a beautifully written, magnificently staged piece of theatre that has thoroughly deserved every success it has enjoyed.
Theatrevibe, the site that doesn't do stars, awards Warhorse five stars for its strong impact of the reality of war and five stars for the state of the art beautiful horses.

cn.t: War Horse remains a theatrical masterpiece nearly 20 years on, with critics praising its groundbreaking puppetry and devastating emotional power. The National Theatre revival proves the show has lost none of its impact or ability to move audiences.
